name: Microsoft for Education Daily
tldr: Wales' Hwb gets a new look with Microsoft 365 still free at home, GitHub Desktop handles more than one account, and new Teams releases need iOS or iPadOS 18 from mid-December.
window: Window: the 24 hours to 05:00 AEDT, Sat 21 Nov 2026 (Friday 20 Nov in the US).
notes: A quiet day for education-specific news: Hwb is the window's education story; the week's other education news (Microsoft Classroom, Study and Learn assignments, Hour of AI) was covered 18-20 Nov. This week: Teams' iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 notice (MC1556088, 17 Nov, as reported by Neowin and XDA), automatic Windows 11 26H2 delivery (18 Nov) and RDMA over USB4 (19 Nov).

Coming, not shipped: Teams' last-read channels (due February 2027), the notetaker bot list and Edge's idle updates (due January 2027) are roadmap items in development; RDMA over USB4 is a developer preview coming soon to Windows Insiders; Edge's Prompt API is an origin trial; Teams guest-invite reporting is rolling out.
Screenshots are the publishers' public pages as captured on 21 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

post.text:
USE WHAT YOU HAVE. 💻

The last 24h at Microsoft for education:
- Wales' Hwb gets a new look; Microsoft 365 at home stays free
- GitHub Desktop: more than one account per host
- Foundry Managed Compute is generally available
- Teams needs iOS/iPadOS 18+ from mid-Dec

stories.title: Wales' Hwb platform gets a new look, and Microsoft 365 at home stays free
stories.summary: Hwb, Wales' education web platform, has been redesigned with feedback from teachers and learners: clearer navigation, easier access to key services and a more personal experience in Welsh and English. Learners and teachers can still install Microsoft 365 (Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Teams) on personal devices at no cost.
stories.for: Learners, teachers and families in Wales

stories.title: Teams will open busy channels at your last read message
stories.summary: Roadmap item 579890, in development: on Teams for desktop and Mac you'll be able to choose to open a channel at your last read message instead of the newest one, so it's easier to catch up on a busy class channel without losing your place. Due February 2027.
stories.for: Students and teachers in class channels

stories.title: Report suspicious guest invitations straight from Teams
stories.summary: When an unexpected or possibly malicious guest invitation arrives in Teams, people can report it to their IT admin for review, on desktop, Mac and web. The roadmap lists it as rolling out, with general availability due in November 2026.
stories.for: Students and staff, with school IT reviewing reports

stories.title: GitHub Desktop now signs in to more than one account on the same host
stories.summary: GitHub Desktop 3.7.0 lets you add more than one account for GitHub.com, GitHub Enterprise Server or GHE.com, with no fixed limit, and ties each repository to the right account for cloning, publishing and other Git operations. A student could keep a personal and a university account side by side (our example).

stories.title: A coming Windows preview links PCs over USB4 to run one bigger AI model
stories.summary: RDMA over USB4 lets two or more USB4 PCs, joined by cables, split one AI model and combine their memory and GPUs, with no RDMA network card or switch. In Microsoft's lab, three mini PCs ran a 235-billion-parameter model at about 18.5 tokens a second. The developer preview is coming soon to Windows Insiders; use dedicated test PCs.

stories.title: Foundry Managed Compute is generally available for open models
stories.summary: Microsoft Foundry's Managed Compute serves 150+ open models on dedicated NVIDIA A100, H100 or H200 or AMD MI300X GPUs, with Global and US or EU Data Zone deployments. You pick the model and pay hourly per GPU; Microsoft provisions the GPUs and runs the serving software.

stories.title: Web developers can now try Edge's built-in AI model, Aion, on live sites
stories.summary: Aion Instruct, a 2.3-billion-parameter open-weights model, is now generally available as Edge's built-in small language model, replacing Phi-4-mini, and a Prompt API origin trial lets developers use it on their live sites. A Decisions API is in developer preview, and users can turn on-device AI off in Edge settings.
stories.status: Aion GA; Prompt API origin trial

stories.title: Teams will let admins choose which outside notetaker bots join meetings
stories.summary: Roadmap item 580451, in development: admins will be able to list the external meeting notetaker bots allowed to join meetings their organisation hosts, and block all others or keep them in the lobby. Allowed bots are treated like any external participant. Due January 2027.

stories.title: Edge will install pending updates while the browser is idle
stories.summary: Roadmap item 581801, in development: Microsoft Edge applies pending updates when the browser is idle, and the Relaunch Notification policy lets IT manage those idle restarts. Due January 2027.

stories.title: New Teams releases will need iOS or iPadOS 18 from mid-December
stories.summary: Microsoft told admins (MC1556088) that Teams support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 ends from mid-December 2026, completing in early January 2027. Copies already installed keep working, with no block on opening or signing in, but newer releases need iOS or iPadOS 18 or later. Admins should find devices on 17 and update MDM minimum-OS policies.
stories.for: School IT with older iPads and iPhones

stories.title: Windows 11 26H2 now installs automatically on PCs that IT doesn't manage
stories.summary: Since 18 November, Microsoft has been gradually expanding automatic delivery of Windows 11 version 26H2 to PCs on 24H2 and 25H2 that aren't managed by an IT department, such as students' and staff's own PCs. Anyone eligible can still get it now from Settings > Windows Update.
stories.for: Students and staff with their own PCs

stories.title: Next week on Xbox: cozy factories, mirrored cats and slime puzzles
stories.summary: Coming to Xbox: Jaden Industries: Cozy Automation Puzzler, a relaxing factory-building puzzle game, on 23 November; Cat Mirror, where you steer two cats with every move mirrored, and Sokobear Goo, with 40 puzzle levels, on 25 November; and Gravity SWITCH, with 50 stages, on 26 November. Release dates are subject to change.

transcript.t: Welcome to the Microsoft for Education Daily, Saturday edition.
Let's catch you up on everything new from Microsoft.
Use what you have. In Wales, the schools platform Hwb just got a fresh, simpler look.
Plus, learners and teachers still get Microsoft 365 free on their own devices.
In class, Teams will let you open a busy channel at your last read message, due February.
Odd guest invite?
You can now report it to IT straight from Teams, as it rolls out.
Coding class?
GitHub Desktop now signs in to more than one account on the same site.
Keep personal and uni accounts side by side; each repo knows which to use.
For university AI labs, a coming Windows preview links PCs with USB4 cables.
In Microsoft's lab, three mini PCs ran a 235-billion-parameter model together.
Prefer the cloud? Foundry's Managed Compute, for open models, is now generally available.
And web developers can now try Edge's built-in AI model, Aion, on a live site.
For school IT, Teams will let you pick which outside notetaker bots join your meetings, due January.
And Edge will install waiting updates when the browser's idle, also due January.
The fine print? From mid-December, new Teams releases need iOS or iPadOS 18 or later.
And personal Windows 11 PCs are now getting 26H2 automatically, bit by bit.
After hours, build tiny factories on floating islands in Jaden Industries, out November 23.
Then Cat Mirror has you steer two cats at once, and every move is mirrored.
Plus Sokobear Goo, with 40 puzzle levels, and Gravity SWITCH, with 50 stages.
A home laptop, spare PCs, the accounts you've got: use what you have.
Every day, the changelog gets a little longer.
Check the board: shipped today, and more on the way.
All of that, in one day. And it keeps on shipping.
That's the Microsoft for Education Daily for today.
Go build something. See you tomorrow.
